title: Restore validation harness for index warmup and read-after-write checks
creator: Marcus Bell
description:
Goal: Build a deterministic restore-validation harness that verifies dataset integrity, index warmup behavior, and read-after-write correctness during active->passive promotions and scheduled failover drills.

Scope:
- Restore a region snapshot into an isolated staging cluster (VPC-isolated) using the exact restore path customers would use.
- Run index warmup sequences (prefix cache priming, embedding/kv cache seeding, model KV prefetch) and measure time-to-warm (target <180s for default 100M token footprint).
- Execute read-after-write (RAW) check suite across affected services (auth tokenstore, routing table, token billing ledger, and user metadata) to confirm no staleness or split-brain.
- Surface pass/fail results to the DR dashboard and emit a machine-readable verdict for drill orchestration.

Acceptance criteria:
1) Restore completes and passes checksum verification for all snapshots (sha256 match) within expected window for region size.
2) Index warmup (measured by 95th percentile API latency returning to baseline) completes within configured SLO window or triggers controlled load-shedding.
3) RAW suite detects 0 mismatched writes and returns consistent reads after the last committed write across 99.99% of samples.
4) Harness emits a JSON verdict and artifacts: restore.log, warmup.metrics, raw-results.json, and a signed snapshot-assertion for audit.

Components produced:
- restore-validator service (k8s job + small CLI): github.com/redwood/inference/restore-validator (draft PR #4392)
- test vectors and RAW generator: s3://redwood-dr-tests/raw-vectors/2026-01
- Confluence playbook with explicit step commands and rollback runbook: https://confluence.redwood.com/display/OPS/DR+Restore+Validation+Harness

Operational notes / trade-offs:
- We avoid running full production write traffic during validation to prevent billing noise; instead we run a deterministic RAW generator that replays recorded write traces and verifies read consistency. This reduces realism slightly but is safer for scheduled drills.
- For very large snapshots we provide an option to run a staged warmup (hot-prefix first) to reduce consecutive memory pressure; that requires a pre-computed prefix-ranking file which is produced by the profiling job.

Next steps:
- Run the harness in the 2026-03 scheduled drill window for eu-west-1 (owner: Lina Park).
- Polish PR #4392: add better exit codes and artifact upload retry logic.
- Add an output hook to the DR dashboard so runbooks automatically link to the latest restore artifacts.
comments: 2026-01-15 - Marcus Bell: Scoped initial acceptance criteria and added pricing/operational constraints. Linked the draft Confluence playbook and the S3 test vectors. Assigned to Lina for implementation.

2026-01-28 - Lina Park: Prototype restore-validator CLI merged to feature branch. Observed that for 1.2TB snapshots index warmup exceeded 4x the target when using a naive full-scan prefetch; switched to prefix-first strategy. See PR: https://github.com/redwood/inference/pull/4392 (WIP).

2026-02-05 - SRE Rotation (Diego Ramos): Added instrumentation hooks to emit warmup.percentile_* metrics and a new DR channel in PagerDuty for failed-verdicts. Draft alert rules added to ops-monitoring: https://grafana.redwood.com/d/ops/dr-restore-validation

2026-02-18 - Lina Park: RAW generator updated to include idempotency checks, sequence numbers, and multi-shard verification. Early runs show a 0.025% transient mismatch rate tied to eventual-consistent secondary indexes — added a 30s stabilization window in the runner.

2026-02-27 - Security Review (Aisha Raman): Reviewed artifact upload plan; requested S3 KMS encryption and signed URLs for short-lived access. Confirmed no secret material is stored in artifacts. Marked security_review_required=false.

2026-03-03 - QA (Evan Chu): Performed smoke runs against small snapshots (20GB) — pass. Began long-run validation in staging; observed one failure tied to an out-of-order log replay; proposed change: include logical timestamps in test vectors to enforce causal order during replay.

2026-03-09 - Lina Park: Updated CLI to emit human-readable summary and machine verdict (pass/fail/warn). Scheduling this harness as part of 2026-03-17 failover drill for eu-west-1. Follow-ups: add dashboard widget and hook into drill orchestration for automatic rollback if verdict==fail.
